newsitem.title: PERU: Lima stocks close lower amid foreign apathy.
newsitem.headline: Lima stocks close lower amid foreign apathy.

text.p: Lima stocks closed slightly lower Tuesday amid apathy by foreign investors, pessimism over imminent economic indicators and poor third-quarter corporate results, brokers said.
Bargain-hunting by local investors prevented heavier declines, they added.
The General Index .IGRA fell 0.67 percent to 1,473.66 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index .ISEL dipped 0.53 percent to 2,039.76.
Brokers expected moderate declines on Wednesday.
Total market volume on Tuesday was a low 24.3 million soles ($9.49 million) on 1,869 trades, as 35 stocks fell, 31 were unchanged and 17 gained.
"The market was apathetic today, waiting for the results of the U.S. elections," said Manuel Torres of Finvest brokerage.
Among leaders, benchmark Telefonica del Peru gained 0.37 percent to 5.41 soles on 1.4 million shares, and mining company Minsur rose 3.09 percent to 22.99 soles on 41,631 shares.
However, mining concern Morococha fell two percent to 1.47 soles on 82,475 shares, while Compania Nacional de Cerveza slipped 1.32 percent to 1.49 soles on 330,887 shares.
